transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because for the last few weeks, I’ve barely had an appetite. It's just... even the foods I usually look forward to eating after a shift, they just sit there in front of me. I pretty much just have to force down a few bites, and that's about it.
Aside from your appetite, have you been feeling down, depressed, or hopeless lately?

Yeah, I have. It's like... most days I just feel like I'm carrying this heavy, flat feeling around with me. Even when I'm home with my family, or just sitting in the break room on my shift, it feels like I'm just not really there.
Have you ever felt this way for a period of time before these last few weeks, perhaps months or years ago?

No, not really. I mean, everyone has a bad day or gets stressed out sometimes, but... no, nothing like this. I've never felt this flat for this long before. It's really just been these last few weeks that it hit me.
Have you found it difficult to experience pleasure or interest in the activities you usually enjoy?

Yeah, I have. I used to really look forward to my morning runs, or playing my guitar, even just cooking dinner. But lately, I keep skipping all of that. They just feel like chores now, and... I just can't seem to get myself to care about doing them anymore.
How has your sleep been lately?
It's been fine, honestly. I haven't really noticed any problems with it. I mean, I just go to bed and sleep about the same amount I always have. So... yeah, no real changes there.
How much have these symptoms interfered with your ability to perform your daily work tasks or manage your household responsibilities?

Well, I’m still showing up and getting the basics done. But... it is starting to affect my job in a way it never used to. I work in surveillance, and lately I've made a few documentation mistakes. I actually missed a surveillance cue recently and ended up getting a formal warning for it. So, yeah, it's definitely getting in the way at work.

Given the mistakes you've made at work and your loss of interest in your hobbies, would you say these symptoms make it very difficult for you to continue your normal social and work activities, or are you still managing to get by despite them?

I think I'm still managing to get by, for the most part. I mean, I'm still showing up and paying the bills. It's not like I've completely stopped functioning or anything. It's just... it's definitely harder than it used to be. I wouldn't say it's impossible to do my job or be around people, it just takes a lot more effort to push through the shift right now.
